_note: Hand-maintained project data: stage status and risks. Each 'completed' stage must name its evidence (files in this repository). Update when a stage changes; the dashboard is rebuilt from this file plus generated evidence.

risks.title: Dashboard traffic results understate G3 / G4 and outer bearings
risks.plain: By default the dashboard puts the two traffic lanes against the left kerb and never moves them. Moving them across the road, G4's traffic moment is 33 % higher and some bearing reactions 1.5-3 times higher.
risks.why: Any design taken from the dashboard's default traffic run for G3, G4 or the outer bearings may be unconservative.

risks.title: Dashboard traffic overstates inner bearings
risks.plain: The dashboard's way of spreading wheel loads onto nodes sends load along whole lines straight into four bearings. Inner bearing reactions come out up to 44 % high and girder moments 1-6 % low.
risks.why: Bearing design from the dashboard is conservative there, girder moments slightly unconservative.

risks.title: BR13A support-line bearing waits for your acceptance
risks.plain: The geometry needs the support-line bearing (44.029166° from the skew diagram). It was only in a note, so the agent proposed it as decision D-34. Until accepted, BR13A geometry is labelled provisional.
risks.why: All girder positions depend on it.

risks.title: BR13A Super-T shape, haunch, cross girder and end blocks wait for your acceptance
risks.plain: The agent proposed the full Super-T shape (D-35, incl. the 90 mm top flange the import missed), a placeholder haunch of 0 mm (D-36), the cross girder 800 x 1065 (D-37, from your query answer) and 2.0 m solid end blocks (D-38, interpretation pending).
risks.why: Section stiffness depends on both; sections are provisional until accepted.

risks.title: MIDAS file needs your import test
risks.plain: The platform now writes the BR13A model as a MIDAS .mct. Bearing links and soil springs use a syntax no one has confirmed in MIDAS yet, and the SDL loads are not in the file.
risks.why: Until imported once, the file may not open or may misread the links / springs.

risks.title: Dashboard earthquake mass is about 10 % too high
risks.plain: The dashboard's modal analysis also weights the deck strips, whose weight is already in the girders. Periods come out up to ~9 % long.
risks.why: Affects the dashboard's earthquake results; the new platform analysis does not do this.

risks.title: BR13A bearing positions disagree between drawings
risks.plain: The abutment drawings place the bearings 50–530 mm away from where the GA girder setout puts them. The model uses the GA positions for now.
risks.why: Bearing positions set where the girders sit on the abutment; the right drawing must be confirmed.

risks.title: BR13A bearing height does not fit the drawn levels
risks.plain: The drawn bearing seats are 100–127 mm below the girder soffit, but the placeholder bearing height is 150 mm (haunch also a 0 mm placeholder). The model uses the drawn levels.
risks.why: Needs the bearing schedule and the haunch to close the vertical geometry.

risks.title: Substructure inputs D-39, D-40, D-41 wait for your acceptance
risks.plain: Sill beam setout and bearing seat levels were copied from the abutment takeoff into the bridge data; the elastomer layer thickness (12 mm) is a placeholder.
risks.why: Until accepted, the integrated model is provisional.

risks.title: Girder end region over-utilised in the current design run
risks.plain: Near the bearings (x = 0.75 m) bending and shear/torsion utilisation exceed 1.0. The end zone (solid end block) is not defined, and strands are placeholders.
risks.why: Could be a real design issue or a missing input; it must be resolved before any girder design is relied on.

risks.title: No result is independently verified yet
risks.plain: All numbers are reproducible outputs of the current software. None has been checked against an independent model.
risks.why: Software tests passing does not mean the bridge results are right.

risks.title: 177 assumed input values in BR13A
risks.plain: Placeholders let the model run; each needs data or an engineer decision.

risks.title: Strand and bar layout are placeholders
risks.plain: A standard T4 layout is used because the BR13A strand drawings are not in the set.
risks.why: Design capacities and stresses depend on them.

risks.title: Design engine neutral axis differs from the worked example
risks.plain: Capacity matches but the neutral-axis depth is about 8 % off.
risks.why: Indicates an engine difference that may matter in other cases.

risks.title: Code-standard values not yet verified
risks.plain: 63 code-standard values are now inventoried in one place (standards/REVIEW_REGISTER.md), but none is verified against an authorised copy; 27 need specialist interpretation.
risks.why: Every design action depends on them.

risks.title: Analysis model is a fixed BR13A file
risks.plain: The model is not yet generated from bridge data.
risks.why: Blocks use on any other bridge.

risks.title: Simplified load combination envelopes
risks.plain: Traffic moment, shear and torsion are enveloped separately; earthquake results are unsigned.
risks.why: Can be conservative or, for some checks, not concurrent.

risks.title: Some plots draw invalid coordinates
risks.plain: 88 drawing errors per run (no calculation error).
risks.why: A plot may show wrong or missing lines.

risks.title: Dashboard model bearing nodes are off the support line by up to 26 mm
risks.plain: The old frozen model places bearings slightly off the printed straight support line. The new geometry engine uses the exact line.
risks.why: Small, but the analysis model should be rebuilt on the exact geometry (stage P3).
